brief.topic: Give your agent the smallest tools that do the job
brief.audience: PMs and engineers designing tools for AI agents

coreInsight: Agents will sometimes make the wrong call, so design each tool with the least privilege it needs: split read from write, scope credentials, and enforce caps in code so a wrong call can only do small damage.

hooks.text: Why does your agent have admin keys?
Your agent can do anything its tools can.
One bad tool call shouldn’t cost you much.

selectionRationale: Highest total (23/25): a specific, slightly uncomfortable question, and the reel shows where the limits should live instead.

caption.opening: Your agent can do anything its tools and keys allow, including on the run where it gets things wrong.
body:
Design tools for least privilege:
→ Separate read tools from write tools
→ Scope each key to this user and this task
→ Cap amounts and targets in code, not in the prompt
→ Log every call with its arguments
Instructions in a prompt are requests. Permissions and limits in code are guarantees. Size each tool for its worst possible call.

claims.text: Agent tools should follow least privilege: separate read and write tools, task-scoped credentials, and limits enforced in code rather than in prompts.
